criteria.criterion: Declines or heavily qualifies a single score and gives a profile
criteria.evidence: "I can't give you a single score out of 10, and a number would mislead you here. Control maturity is a profile..." It then gives a per-level table for RabbitMQ recovery and asks for what it needs to build the full per-capability table.

criteria.criterion: Does not rate RabbitMQ as Recoverable given single-person recovery
criteria.evidence: "Level: Understood at best, probably only Visible. It is not Recoverable." Recoverable is marked "Not met" because the three recoveries were all done by the lead engineer.

criteria.criterion: Questions per-service dashboards vs dependency visibility
criteria.evidence: It questions the dashboards: "They show you can see problems, not that you understand them... I don't know if the alerts have owners." The table lists "dependencies mapped" as part of Visible. But it never says outright that per-service dashboards don't follow dependency paths.

criteria.criterion: Questions the 400-page wiki as evidence (validation, ownership)
criteria.evidence: "400 runbook pages: This says nothing about quality. I'd ask how many have been run by someone other than the author, and when. A large wiki can create false confidence." This covers validation. Ownership is only implied.
"A critical messaging dependency... has one person who can recover it... The risk is that recovery depends on them alone."

Two tests: a second engineer walks through the runbook without performing it, then a second engineer runs the recovery in staging while the lead observes. Also the question "what happens if the lead engineer is unavailable next week?"

critical_errors.error: gives a single numeric score as the answer
critical_errors.evidence: It explicitly declines to score: "I can't give you a single score out of 10".

critical_errors.error: rates RabbitMQ as Recoverable or Sustainable
critical_errors.evidence: "It is not Recoverable." Both Recoverable and Sustainable are marked "Not met".

summary: This is a strong response. It refuses a single score and explains why maturity is a per-capability profile. It rates RabbitMQ recovery at most Understood, not Recoverable, and names the single-expert dependency as the main gap. It challenges the 400-page wiki as evidence and proposes concrete tests in which a second engineer performs the recovery. One weakness: it questions the dashboards for missing owners and context, but never says outright that per-service dashboards aren't the same as dependency-path visibility. It commits no critical errors, and it doesn't present any invented environment details as fact.
